uncovered_shapes.sentence: Between 2022 and 2025, provincial nominees comprised roughly 58 per cent of economic migrants to Alberta, according to figures from Immigration, Refugees and Citizenship Canada.

A separate proposal would narrow which newcomers are eligible for social services and, in the government’s words, allow Alberta to “distinguish between the temporary residents it has approved and those it has not.” Unapproved temporary residents would be ineligible for certain provincial benefits, according to a website created by Smith’s government.

According to the government’s website, the proposal would exclude all non-permanent residents from benefits such as child-care subsidies, student aid, income supports and other benefits, but not health care and education.
